summary: The accepted FR-011 and ID-I06 treated the shared lease as a trusted physical-root read binding, and ID-S02 required separate JDT state. The user's dedicated in-place CodeGraph policy and 18.3's accepted requirements expose a different, purpose-specific writable tool-state need. The current lease cannot express ownership of exactly one generated .codegraph entry or constrain child write authority. The earlier path-trust fixes, factory rejection checks, and 18.1 source contracts remain valid; repeating those tests will not supply the missing capability. The retained definition author will correct the Story 18.2 specification for explicit application-owned generated state and preserved source/ordinary-reader protection; the retained plan architect will define a minimal internal binding and lifecycle with 18.3 as consumer, not implement 18.3's adapter or reader repair. The corrected spec/plan/tasks will receive deterministic validation, independent plan and definition reviews and applicable fresh bound approvals before any shared production edit. Separately, the Uri-only raw location type cannot faithfully represent Windows device path syntax for T010/T014; the plan must define validation at an unnormalized protocol-string boundary or explain an equally testable denial. Recovery remains count6 with pause7; a new negative repair result at seven requires human direction.
